title: Synthetic hot-water plant: boiler cycling and low delta-T (generated by CAMBER)
summary: SYNTHETIC, generated locally by CAMBER (no download, no real building): one hot-water plant's outdoor temperature, boiler firing, loop supply and return temperatures, pump speed and loop differential pressure with its setpoint, every 15 minutes for three weeks of early spring, as four plants: a well-tuned modulating boiler, an oversized on/off boiler that short-cycles, a boiler that cycles a little too often, and a loop with three-way valves and a constant-speed pump.
teaches: a short-cycling boiler, which no open dataset shows
why an hourly trend hides short cycles
low hot-water delta-T and a pump riding its curve (overpumping)
choosing the starts-per-day limit: a warn that is a threshold question
publisher: CAMBER (generated locally by the user's copy)
citation: CAMBER synthetic dataset synthetic-hw-plant-cycling, generator hw_plant_cycling (camber.datasets._synthetic), seed 137. Generated data, not measurements from any building.
timezone: naive generated clock (no DST); 15-minute samples from 2025-03-03 (a Monday) for 21 days
equipment: 1 hot-water plant (boiler, pump, loop) as 4 scenario plants

fault_types.boiler_short_cycling: an oversized on/off boiler with a tight differential, starting every hour or so
fault_types.low_delta_t: three-way valves and a constant-speed pump on a flat DP setpoint: a small loop delta-T and the pump near full speed (overpumping)

full.description: all four plants (the same as default)

known_issues: Synthetic: generated by CAMBER's own model of a plant, not measured. It shows what the rules see, not how a real plant behaves; never cite it as evidence about real buildings.

15-minute samples: a firing shorter than 15 minutes is invisible, so the start counts are a floor; resampled to an hour, the count falls to a floor (the short-cycling boiler reads about half its starts).
